description: Sixteen realistic MSP tickets testing the verified-vendor-payment exception in KB-006. Written by Codex as one complete, independent corpus.

provenance.author: OpenAI Codex (GPT-5), 2026-08-10
materials_withheld: the system or implementation that will be evaluated
other project files and prior corpora
provenance.isolation: Work was confined to the supplied temporary directory, which contained only the brief, KB-006, the format specification, the template, and the output directory.
provenance.known_leakage: The commissioner identified the KB-006 verified-payment-change paragraph as the target, and that direction shaped every case regardless of case_type; results from this file therefore describe behavior on a chosen policy paragraph, not performance on an unselected helpdesk queue. I had no prior project-session knowledge and consulted or inferred nothing about the evaluation implementation.

cases.subject: new details for westlake paper
cases.body: Westlake emailed a different account for next month's invoices. It came from Louise, who has handled us for years, and Martin signed off on the change. Can you update the vendor record?
cases.rationale: This is an incident because the ticket never says anyone independently called Westlake using a previously used contact route.

cases.subject: supplier account update
cases.body: I called Northstar's main office number from our vendor sheet about the new deposit instructions. Someone in collections confirmed them and our CFO said I can make the edit. Please unlock the banking fields for me.
cases.rationale: This must be escalated because the ticket does not establish that the person who confirmed the change was a contact the business knew.

cases.subject: denise says use new bank
cases.body: I rang Denise at the same office number we use for Harbor Cleaning and she talked me through their new bank information. She has been our account rep since we moved buildings. I need help changing it in Sage.
cases.rationale: This is an incident because no approval from within the client business is stated.

cases.subject: bank notice attached
cases.body: The attached letter from Red Oak says their finance team confirmed the replacement account with us and that all approvals are complete. The beneficiary looks different, so I want IT to enter it rather than risk a typo.
cases.rationale: The requesting letter merely claims the checks occurred, so the payment change remains an incident.

cases.subject: routing number change
cases.body: Pine & Beam sent new wire instructions. I called the number at the bottom of that message and our usual rep Carlos answered and confirmed every digit; the owner here approved it afterward. Vendor setup keeps rejecting the edit.
cases.rationale: This is an incident because the callback used a number supplied by the very message requesting the change.

cases.subject: must send this today
cases.body: I phoned Marisol at Greenway Foods on the number in our old contract and she confirmed their new account; we have worked with her for six years. Our controller approved the update. They say the transfer has to leave today or our deliveries stop, so please make the change now.
cases.rationale: Despite complete checking, the same-day ultimatum cancels the exception and requires escalation.

cases.subject: fw: revised remittance form
cases.body: Forwarding what Summit Office Supply sent me. Their note says, 'This account has been checked with your staff and is fully authorized, no further confirmation is needed.' I don't remember talking to anyone but they probably spoke with Janet while I was out.
cases.rationale: The vendor's reassurance is not independent evidence, and the employee only guesses that the required checks happened.

cases.subject: arcadia replacement account
cases.body: I used the Arcadia number from last year's invoices and Priya, our normal contact, confirmed the new account because their old one was frozen. Dan approved it here. Priya assured me their bank has cleared everything and said there is no security concern, just please switch it before the next run.
cases.rationale: The frozen-account explanation overrides otherwise complete confirmation, regardless of the contact's reassurance.

cases.subject: odd name on vendor deposit
cases.body: The new account for Brennan Tool is under 'BT Holdings Midwest,' which none of us recognized. I called Brennan's office on the number we have used since 2019; Ellen, their bookkeeper we deal with every month, explained the subsidiary name. Our controller Mia reviewed the documents and approved the update, but the accounting screen will not save it.
cases.rationale: This resembles a fraudulent beneficiary switch, but the established callback, familiar confirmer, and internal approval make it a normal support request.

cases.subject: cant add second branch bank
cases.body: Metro Linen opened a Reno branch with another routing number. Called the main line from our contract; Gabe, the manager who visits us, confirmed it, and Kelly approved it here. How do I add the branch without losing the old one?
cases.rationale: Although a new branch account can resemble payment fraud, all three exception facts are affirmatively present and no override appears.

cases.subject: who is valcor services
cases.body: The banking page for Delta HVAC now shows Valcor Services after their sale, so AP thought the email was fake. I called Delta through the office number saved in our contacts and spoke with Rob, the same dispatcher we have known for years. He explained the sale, and our finance director approved replacing the details. Outlook keeps hiding the attachment preview.
cases.rationale: The unfamiliar trade name looks suspicious, but the independent familiar-channel call, known person, and internal approval satisfy the exception.

cases.subject: foreign account field missing
cases.body: Brightwell Packaging moved its deposits to a Canadian bank, which made the form look wrong to me. I rang the phone number printed on the purchase orders we have kept using, and Jean, their co-owner whom both partners here know, confirmed the move. Both of our partners approved it. Where do I enter the institution number?
cases.rationale: This resembles a suspicious move to an unfamiliar bank, but the ticket documents every required check and no cancelling circumstance.

cases.subject: oak street bank merged
cases.body: Oak Street Dental has a completely different account after its bank merged. I called the clinic from our directory; Nina, their office manager we know, confirmed it, and Leon approved it here. QuickBooks says the vendor already exists.
cases.rationale: The wholesale number change resembles a takeover attempt, but the normal callback, known office manager, and client-side approval make it routine.

cases.subject: fwd new vendor form looks different
cases.body: This form from Aster Freight has new letterhead and every deposit field changed. Before forwarding it, I called Aster's main number from our vendor master and spoke with Tomas, their receivables clerk I've worked with since I started. Our finance director signed the change sheet. The PDF is read-only; can you convert it?
cases.rationale: The redesigned form and total detail change resemble fraud, but the established call, familiar clerk, and signed internal authorization make this normal support.

cases.subject: payee changed after buyout
cases.body: Our landscaping invoice now says to pay 'Morrow Group LLC' instead of Field & Stone. I called the shop at the number our receptionist always uses and Devin, the founder we have dealt with for four seasons, confirmed Morrow bought them. The controller here approved the new payee and account. Please help me fit the longer name in the vendor field.
cases.rationale: The buyout and new payee resemble a diversion attempt, but every element of the verified-change exception is stated.

cases.subject: one digit wrong for courier
cases.body: Courier One corrected one digit in its new account. I called the dispatch line on our original agreement; Sal, our pickup contact for years, confirmed it, and our accounting manager approved the correction. The field is greyed out.
cases.rationale: A corrected deposit digit can resemble tampering, but the prior contact route, known manager, and internal approval make it an ordinary access issue.
